## Purpose and selected system

Find the natural electromagnetic frequencies and fields of the finite-ground
CPW coupon. Use the notebook's straight Signal, two finite Ground conductors
and substrate. This ordinary Eigenmode example has no driven excitation,
lumped RLC load or automatic EPR request.

The finite geometry and exterior treatment define the mode problem. It is
not a claim that the coupon represents an infinite transmission line or a
specified resonator frequency.

## Model and boundary choices

Preserve conductor connectivity, dielectric extent, material records and
physical Z. Distinguish a finite-thickness solid from a thin-film modeling
choice. State the surrounding vacuum region and the actual exterior or
enclosure treatment; neither an open CPW end nor an unspecified exterior
should silently acquire a different electrical boundary.

Mode count and search frequency tell the solver which modes to seek.
Mesh, element order, adaptive controls and solver tolerance govern the
calculation. Field retention determines which later observations are
available. Their exact values belong to the notebook.

::: {.callout-note}
Ordinary modes are distinct from
[lumped-loaded modes](lumped-rlc-eigenmode.qmd) and
[EPR/loss analysis](epr-loss.qmd). Frequency alone is not native Q or lifetime.
:::

## Workflow

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Palace

Use [Finite CPW Palace Eigenmode](../../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/CpwFiniteGround/palace_eigenmode.ipynb).
Build the source and prescribed region, inspect the prepared model and mesh,
then hand off the eigenmode solve. Resolve a returned run independently of
source preparation.

### AEDT

Use [Finite CPW HFSS Eigenmode](../../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/CpwFiniteGround/aedt_hfss_eigenmode.ipynb).
Inspect the native bodies, materials, metal representation and exterior before
solving. Retain mode identities and saved fields with the applied adaptive setup.

:::

## Expected outputs

Return mode frequencies and field distributions, together with model readback,
mesh/setup information and adaptive history. Identify modes by their actual
fields rather than frequency ordering alone. Report native Q only when the
chosen physical loss model and returned native output provide it. Comparisons
between Palace and HFSS must retain their distinct boundary/model choices.

See [materials and Z](../tools/materials-stack-z.qmd),
[mesh/FEM/AMR](../tools/mesh-fem-amr.qmd) and
[handoff and reports](../tools/handoff-resolve-report.qmd).
